historical_reviews.deepseek: Selects a diag token without knowing which environment or workload starts, what result is expected or how it exits safely; credentials, readback and recovery are also missing.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires the vendor diagnostic definition and safety envelope before converting the boot target into an executable test.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Booting to diagnostics and passing diagnostics are separate checkpoints. First prove the expected environment identity/version; then run only the explicitly approved module set, because some diagnostic menus default to burn-in or destructive storage tests.

original_test_intent: Validate the one-time Diags boot target by reaching the intended vendor diagnostic environment and completing only its owner-approved bounded, non-destructive diagnostic scope before restoring normal boot.
original_method: Define the exact built-in or media-based diagnostic environment, version, module selection, resource limits, expected result and abort procedure; capture platform baseline, apply/read back the protected one-time Diags override after approval, reboot under console and health monitoring, identify the environment, run only the approved modules, preserve results, exit cleanly, clear the override and restore the original OS path.
manual_activity: The owner defines and approves the diagnostic modules and limits; an operator observes the environment and health, aborts unsafe behavior and controls exit, restoration, recovery and verdict.
required_inputs: Approved diagnostic module list and duration
Expected result dictionary and boot marker
Thermal, power, memory, storage and network limits
safety_requirements: Do not assume diag is read-only or non-destructive
Identify environment and module selection before running anything
Exclude storage writes or uncontrolled burn-in unless separately approved
Use protected credentials and one-time scope
Monitor thermals, power, console and health independently
Stop on wrong environment, unapproved module, write, alarm, hang or timeout
Exit cleanly, clear override and restore baseline
Preserve logs and do not automatically retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate diagnostic identity, result dictionary and safety envelope
Apply/read back one approved one-time Diags setting after confirmation
Request and perform one approved reboot
Collect structured state and bounded diagnostic output under operator supervision
Verify clean exit, override consumption and normal OS health
engineer_actions: Approve exact environment, modules, limits and expected result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: bootdev diag can request a diagnostic class only after vendor mapping; the literal command exposes credentials, resets immediately and says nothing about environment identity, module risk, expected output, abort or restoration.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the protected vendor-mapped one-time Diags control, identify the resulting environment on console, then run only the approved bounded module set with health monitoring before clean exit and restoration.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Diags, Enabled/Save, reboot and 10/20-minute estimates remain for boot validation; any diagnostic duration beyond that requires explicit project definition.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Separate evidence into override-to-environment identity and environment-to-module result, recording version, selected modules, start/stop time, maximum thermals/power, output codes and clean exit.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines what Diags actually launches and constrains its activity while retaining the requested target.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Reaching a diagnostic menu does not prove a diagnostic result, and a result code from an unidentified image cannot prove the intended environment was used.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Vendor diagnostic environments may auto-run burn-in, modify NVRAM or test disks. Their risk cannot be inferred from the generic IPMI diag selector.

project_override_considerations: The Project must specify whether acceptance is boot-to-menu only or also execution of named modules, and must disposition the copied PXE note separately. No unspecified default diagnostic run is allowed.
expected_evidence: Approved target/window, exact diagnostic source/version, module/result matrix and safety envelope
Protected one-time Diags write/readback and reboot request
POST/console proof of the intended diagnostic environment identity
Selected modules, bounded output/result codes and thermal/power/storage observations
Clean exit, consumed override and original OS restoration
Health, diagnostic/audit/SEL/OS logs, recovery actions and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and procedure consistently request Diags boot. The diagnostic specifics are omitted readiness inputs; the PXE note is copied context rather than an alternate target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The vendor diagnostic definition, modules and recovery plan are normal project artifacts that can be requested. Execution must stop if they remain unknown, but review does not require guessing.

review_improvement: Splits vague diagnostic boot into an identity checkpoint and a separately bounded workload/result checkpoint, preventing a generic selector from authorizing unknown stress or writes.
independent_technical_reasoning: A firmware diagnostic target can refer to embedded UEFI code, a service partition or external media, each with different modules and side effects. Therefore the selector value is not the test oracle: console identity and version establish the environment, while a named module/result ledger establishes any diagnostic claim safely.
